form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Schatz (for himself, Mr. Warner, and Mr. Kennedy) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

form.official-title: To enable Federal employees and contractors to correct their credit reports to remove adverse items of information reported as a result of a shutdown, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Protect Federal Workers' Credit Act.
Section 603 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681a) is amended by adding at the end the following:

subsection.text: The term contractor has the meaning given the term in section 7101 of title 41, United States Code.

paragraph.text: the period beginning on the date on which a shutdown begins and ending on the date that is 30 days after the date on which the shutdown ends; and
with respect to the shutdown that began on December 21, 2018, and ended on January 25, 2019, the 60-day period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act.
means an employee of a Government agency that had a lapse in appropriations as a result of a shutdown; and
includes an employee of a contractor that has a contract with a Government agency that had a lapse in appropriations as a result of a shutdown.

subsection.text: The term shutdown means any period in which there is more than a 24-hour lapse in appropriations for any Government agency or Federal department as a result of a failure to enact a regular appropriations bill or continuing resolution that results in a delay or loss of payment or wages to a Federal worker.
The term small business concern has the meaning given the term in section 3 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632).

section.header: Limitation on furnishing an adverse item of information resulting from the shutdown
section.text: Section 623 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681s–2) is amended by adding at the end the following:

subsection.header: Limitation on furnishing adverse information resulting from a shutdown
subsection.text: A person shall not furnish any adverse item of information relating to a consumer during a covered period to any consumer reporting agency if the person has been notified by the consumer that—

paragraph.text: the ability of the consumer to make an on-time payment during the covered period has been materially affected by a shutdown; or
the late or missed payment by the consumer during the covered period was a result of a shutdown.

section.header: Prohibition on including an adverse item of information in consumer reports
section.text: Section 605(a) of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681c(a)) is amended by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: An adverse item of information reported to the consumer reporting agency relating to a consumer during a covered period if—

subparagraph.text: the consumer is a Federal worker listed in the database described in section 611(h)(2); or
the consumer has successfully requested the removal of an adverse item of information contained in the consumer's file pursuant to the process described in section 611(h)(4).

section.header: Process for deleting negative information from consumer reports
section.text: The Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.) is amended—

subparagraph.text: in clause (v), by striking and at the end;
in clause (vi), by striking the period at the end and inserting ; and; and
by adding at the end the following:

clause.text: the right of a consumer to—

subclause.text: request the deletion of adverse items of information under section 611(h)(4); and
request 2 consumer reports, without charge to the consumer, under section 611(h)(5).

subparagraph.text: in subsection (a)(1)(A), by inserting and subsection (h) before , if the completeness; and
by adding at the end the following:

subsection.header: Deletion of adverse items of information resulting from a shutdown

paragraph.header: Requirement to provide list of impacted Federal workers

subparagraph.text: Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this subsection—

clause.text: each Government agency for which there was a lapse in appropriations during the shutdown that ended on January 25, 2019, shall provide to the Bureau a list of each Federal worker who was furloughed or required to work without pay for any period of time during a shutdown; and
each Federal contractor impacted by the shutdown that ended on January 25, 2019, shall provide to the Bureau a list of each employee whose pay was reduced or delayed as a result of a shutdown.

subparagraph.text: With respect to a shutdown beginning after January 25, 2019, not later than 3 days after the date on which the shutdown ends—

clause.text: each Government agency for which there was a lapse in appropriations shall provide to the Bureau a list of each Federal worker who was furloughed or required to work without pay for any period of time during the shutdown; and
each Federal contractor impacted by the shutdown shall provide to the Bureau a list of each employee whose pay was reduced or delayed as a result of the shutdown.

paragraph.text: The Bureau shall establish and maintain a secure database that—

subparagraph.text: is accessible to consumer reporting agencies described in section 603(p) and nationwide specialty consumer reporting agencies to check and automatically delete any adverse item of information reported during a covered period with respect to a Federal worker under paragraph (3); and
contains the information reported under paragraph (1).

paragraph.header: Deletion of adverse items of information by nationwide consumer reporting and nationwide specialty consumer reporting agencies

subparagraph.text: Each consumer reporting agency described in section 603(p) and each nationwide specialty consumer reporting agency shall, using the information contained in the database established under paragraph (2), delete from the file of each Federal worker named in the database each adverse item of information reported to the agency during the covered period.
Each agency described in subparagraph (A) shall—

clause.text: delete adverse items of information as soon as practicable after information that is reported under paragraph (1) appears in the database established under paragraph (2); and

not later than the date that is 3 days after the end of a covered period, delete any remaining adverse items of information that were reported between the date on which adverse items of information were deleted under clause (i) and the end of the covered period.

paragraph.header: Request for deletion of adverse items of information

subparagraph.text: A consumer who is an employee or owner of a small business concern and who was materially affected by a shutdown may submit a request, without charge to the consumer, to a consumer reporting agency to delete from the consumer's file an adverse item of information reported to the consumer reporting agency during the covered period.
A consumer may submit a request under subparagraph (A)—

clause.text: with respect to the shutdown that ended on January 25, 2019, not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this subsection; and
with respect to a shutdown beginning after January 25, 2019, not later than 90 days after the date on which the shutdown ends.

subparagraph.text: Upon receiving a request under this paragraph to delete an adverse item of information, a consumer reporting agency shall—

clause.text: delete the adverse item of information from the consumer's file if the consumer provides documentation to the consumer reporting agency that the consumer is—

subclause.text: a Federal worker whose pay was delayed or reduced during the covered period; or
an employee or owner of a small business concern who was materially affected by a shutdown; and

clause.text: notify the consumer and the furnisher of the adverse item of information of the deletion.

subparagraph.text: A consumer reporting agency shall make all disclosures pursuant to section 609 twice during the 12-month period following the end of a shutdown upon request by a consumer impacted by the shutdown and without charge to the consumer—

clause.text: with respect to the shutdown that ended on January 25, 2019, if the consumer makes a request within 180 days after the date of enactment of this subsection; and
with respect to a shutdown beginning after January 25, 2019, if the consumer makes a request within 180 days after the date on which the shutdown ends.

subparagraph.text: A consumer reporting agency shall provide a consumer report under subparagraph (A) not later than 15 days after the date on which the request is received under subparagraph (A).
A consumer report provided under subparagraph (A) shall be in addition to any report requested by the consumer under section 612(a).

A consumer reporting agency that receives a request under subparagraph (A) may not request or require any documentation from the consumer that demonstrates that the consumer was impacted by a shutdown as a condition of receiving the consumer report.

paragraph.text: Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, and immediately after the beginning of a shutdown, each consumer reporting agency shall prominently post and maintain a direct link on the homepage of the public website of the consumer reporting agency information relating to the right of consumers to—

subparagraph.text: request the deletion of adverse items of information under paragraph (4); and
request 2 consumer reports, without charge to the consumer, under paragraph (5).
